excerpt: Why the I-95 and US-17 corridor through Darien and Brunswick is among southeast Georgia's most dangerous, and what to do after a crash.
keyTakeaways: The I-95 and US-17 corridor through Darien and Brunswick is one of Southeast Georgia's most dangerous driving environments, with heavy commercial truck traffic, fatigued long-distance travelers, and rural two-lane roads with no median barriers. Georgia's two-year statute of limitations (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and comparative fault rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, less than 50% at fault) apply to crashes in McIntosh and Glynn counties, while federal trucking regulations provide additional grounds for claims against negligent commercial carriers on I-95.

faqs.question: What are the most dangerous roads near Darien, Georgia?
faqs.answer: Interstate 95 and U.S. Highway 17 are the most dangerous roads in the Darien-Brunswick area. I-95 carries enormous volumes of high-speed long-distance and commercial truck traffic through sparsely populated territory with limited emergency response infrastructure. U.S. 17 is a two-lane coastal highway through McIntosh County with no median barriers, limited shoulders, and frequent logging truck traffic.

faqs.question: Why is I-95 so dangerous near Darien and Brunswick?
faqs.answer: The McIntosh and Glynn County segment of I-95 is a through-corridor for travelers and commercial trucks moving between Florida and the northeast. Many drivers are fatigued from long hours on the road, heavy truck traffic from the Port of Savannah and Port of Jacksonville creates dangerous conditions, and the rural setting means emergency response times are longer and trauma centers are farther away.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim after a crash on I-95 in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33, Georgia gives accident victims two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If you are a South Carolina resident injured on I-95 in Georgia, the Georgia two-year deadline applies to your claim. South Carolina allows three years under S.C. Code § 15-3-530 for crashes that occur within its borders.

faqs.question: What makes rural road crashes near Darien different from city crashes?
faqs.answer: Rural crash victims face unique challenges including longer emergency response times, greater distances to trauma centers (the nearest Level 1 center is Memorial Health in Savannah, about 60 miles from Darien), limited traffic camera and surveillance evidence, poor road lighting and conditions, and wildlife strike hazards. These factors can increase both the severity of injuries and the difficulty of proving fault.

faqs.question: Can I sue a trucking company for an I-95 crash near Darien?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a commercial truck driver's negligence caused your crash — including fatigue, hours-of-service violations, distraction, or impairment — you may have claims against both the driver and the trucking company. Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration regulations govern truck driver hours, vehicle maintenance, and driver qualifications, and violations can establish negligence in your injury claim.

faqs.question: Is US-17 being made safer near Brunswick?
faqs.answer: The Georgia Department of Transportation is widening sections of U.S. 17 in northern Glynn County from two lanes to four lanes, which should improve safety once complete. However, the construction itself creates temporary hazards including lane shifts, reduced speeds, and equipment in the roadway. McIntosh County sections of US-17 remain largely two-lane with no current widening plans.
